title: A Near-Optimal Joint Lower Bound for Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
abstract: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number $κ$, the sparsity $s$ of the input matrix, and the target precision $\varepsilon$. The dependence on $κ$ and $\varepsilon$ is already well understood through the lower bound $Ω(κ\log(1/\varepsilon))$, which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity $s$ is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be $Ω(κ\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound $Ω(κ\sqrt{s})$ for constant error $\varepsilon$. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound $Ω(κ\sqrt{s}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.
summary: This paper establishes the near-optimal joint lower bound for quantum query complexity when solving sparse linear systems. By reducing the problem to a hard Boolean function and leveraging the XOR lemma, the authors prove the complexity scales as $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s} \log(1/\epsilon))$. This result is crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum computation in applied areas like optimization and machine learning.
main_problem: To determine the joint quantum query complexity lower bound for solving Quantum Linear Systems (QLS) in the sparse-access model.
main_result: The paper proves the near-optimal joint lower bound of $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s} \log(1/\epsilon))$ for the QLS problem, establishing the dependence on the condition number ($\kappa$), sparsity ($s$), and precision ($\epsilon$).
method: The proof uses a reduction from a hard Boolean query problem (Position-Parity) to the QLS problem, combining results via the XOR lemma and analyzing the resulting structured Hamiltonian matrix.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed in the sparse-access model for QLS, where the input matrix $A$ is $s$-sparse. The complexity is measured by the number of oracle calls required to approximate the solution state $|	ext{x}angle$.
key_observables: Query complexity ($T$), success probability of the decoding procedure, and the adversary bound ($	ext{Adv}_{\pm}(f)$).
important_parameters: Condition number $\kappa$, sparsity $s$, and target error $\epsilon$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Boolean query model reduction and the application of the XOR lemma to combine independent hardness results.
paper_structure: The paper builds complexity bounds by first establishing a $\Omega(\sqrt{m})$ bound for the Position-Parity problem, then constructing a complex QLS instance $H_X$ that encodes $n$ independent instances, and finally using the XOR lemma to combine these results into the final $\Omega(\kappa\sqrt{s} \log(1/\epsilon))$ bound.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical benchmark for quantum algorithms, showing the optimal scaling required for solving linear systems using quantum resources.
